TomTom, Netherlands, presents high-precision speed restrictions for ISA, ADAS, and automation

April 10, 2026 TomTom, speed restrictions, ISA, ADAS, automotive maps
Read the source article

Quick summary

MarkLines highlights TomTom’s Unified Speed Restrictions service as a way for automakers to exceed minimum ISA compliance with fresher, more precise speed data for ADAS and automated driving.

Key takeaways

  • TomTom launched Unified Speed Restrictions as a service aimed at more accurate and current speed-limit information.
  • The offer is positioned against regulatory needs around Intelligent Speed Assistance and broader ADAS performance goals.
  • TomTom argues that minimum compliance is not enough to build driver trust in speed-aware systems.
  • The service is framed as relevant not only for ISA but also for more advanced automated-driving workflows.
  • The MarkLines article is brief because most details sit behind a paywall, but it confirms the automotive-market positioning of the launch.
